title: Model-lock change: automated smoke scheduling and priority routing
creator: Nadia Chen
description:
Background: When a model version is locked in the catalog or a tenant pins a model, we need a low-friction, automated mechanism to run targeted smoke/eval suites that exercise tenant-critical prompts and config combos. Current hand-operated checks cause delays for customers and increase risk of undetected regressions.

Goal: Implement an automated scheduler and priority router that kicks off lightweight smoke/eval runs on model-lock events (catalog-level publishes and tenant model pins). The system should: 1) map the change to relevant eval suites, 2) schedule executors with priority buckets (critical tenants, catalog-wide baseline, low-priority background samples), 3) surface results in the Console with pass/fail and regression deltas, and 4) integrate with rollout policies (canary hold/auto-fallback) for high-risk failures.
scope: Catalog publish events (new model versions added to catalog)
Tenant model pin or upgrade events
Lightweight smoke suites and targeted prompt cohorts
Priority buckets (critical tenants, catalog baseline, background samples)
Console UI callouts and eval result webhooks
out_of_scope: Full-scale long-running evals (these remain in batch pipelines)
proposal: Create an Eval Orchestrator microservice that subscribes to model-change events from the catalog service and tenant configuration events. The orchestrator will use a rules engine to select eval suites and assign a priority score based on tenant SLAs, recent traffic, and sticky prompt examples. A lightweight executor pool will run smoke tests with short timeouts and bounded token budgets. Failures trigger: 1) a Console alert and regression dashboard entry, 2) an optional hold on automated promotion for catalog publishes, and 3) a webhook to tenant ops if the tenant has opted into pre-promotion checks.
implementation_steps: Design event schema for model-lock and tenant-pin events (Eng + Catalog)
Rules engine design: mapping heuristics from model change to eval suites (PM + Research)
Build Eval Orchestrator service and lightweight executor pool (Eng Runtime)
Add priority scoring that considers tenant criticality and recent error rates (Eng + SRE)
Console UI: show per-change smoke summary and quick links to full diffs (DX/Product)
Integrate with rollout policies to optionally block promotions on critical regressions (Product + Infra)
Create webhook and email notification templates for customer-locked pins (Support)
Run pilot with 3 internal tenants and 2 catalog publishes
observability: Per-event trace ids and duration metrics
Pass/fail counts and delta metrics by suite and tenant
Dashboard: recent model-change evaluations and top regressions
Alerting: P0 if critical tenant failure; P1 for catalog-wide regression
acceptance_criteria: On catalog publish, orchestrator runs assigned smoke suites within configured SLAs
Critical-tenant pin events run with higher priority and complete before low-priority background samples start
Console surfaces a summary card within 90s of completion and links to detailed diffs
Rollout policies can be configured to block promotion when critical-suite failure rate exceeds threshold
Pilot tenants confirm decrease in manual validation steps and accept webhook notifications
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overloading executors on busy publish day -> Mitigation: priority queuing + burst autoscaling with limits
Risk: False positives from small smoke suites -> Mitigation: ensemble checks and persistent post-failure longer evals before auto-blocking
Risk: Customer fatigue from many alerts -> Mitigation: rate-limited webhooks and opt-in notification levels per tenant
Risk: Security/exposure of tenant prompts -> Mitigation: run tenant-specific suites inside private-enclave executors for Private deployments
tasks: Finalize event payload and fields by 2026-02-01
Run pilot and collect feedback by 2026-03-31
notes: Design decision: use lightweight smoke suites to balance speed vs signal; longer evaluators live in the batch system for post-hoc analysis.
Trade-off: blocking catalog promotions reduces risk but increases time-to-publish; default will be advisory with opt-in strict mode for high-SLA customers.
We will sample a small percent of tenant pins for full fidelity evals to calibrate smoke-suite thresholds.
